`APPROVED-WITH-CAVEAT`, naming the exact staged-vs-unstaged split and the action needed, rather
than a clean `APPROVED` that would misrepresent what's actually about to be committed.

**Pattern reinforced (now with two same-day instances):** a coordinator's natural-language "only
file X changed, tests still green" claim describes the STATE THEY OBSERVED (usually the working
tree, since that's what `npm test`/editors read), not necessarily what `git diff --cached` holds.
Split the check into two independent facts every re-gate: (1) does the STAGED diff match the claim
— `git diff --cached`, and (2) is `git status` clean of any `M`/`A` + unstaged-tail letter pair on
every touched file. Only rewrite a clean-`APPROVED` marker when both hold; use `APPROVED-WITH-CAVEAT`
(never silently `git add` on the coordinator's behalf) when tests are provably fine but the index
doesn't yet contain what's being described as ready to commit.

### 2026-07-22 — relatedSeriesFor (new pure-data helper): clean, purely-additive test file; sorted-array set-equality can silently un-pin a documented order contract

**Context:** brand-new `src/lib/tv/relatedSeries.ts` (curated static "same TMDB entries =
same fictional series" map, e.g. Doctor Who classic/revival/2024 relaunch) + its first test
file, both newly staged (no prior assertions touched, nothing to weaken). 4/4 pass.

**Approved, with two low-severity nits worth naming as a reusable pattern:**
- **`.map(e => e.id).sort()` vs `[...].sort()` set-equality checks are honest for
  membership, but they discard any order guarantee the production code documents.** Here
  the module comment states results are chronological "so the strip reads left-to-right in
  air order" — but because both sides of the assertion are sorted before comparing, a
  mutation that reverses or shuffles the returned array's order passes unchanged (confirmed
  by reasoning through `filter()`'s order-preserving semantics vs. what the sorted
  comparison can and can't detect). If a helper's doc comment makes an order claim, the test
  should compare the array directly (no `.sort()`) for at least one case, or explicitly note
  order is unspecified/don't-care and drop the claim from the comment.
- **A "non-empty label on every returned entry" loop that only samples ONE query's return
  value doesn't cover every group member's label** — querying only `relatedSeriesFor(RELAUNCH)`
  never returns RELAUNCH's own label (self-excluded), so that string is never asserted
  non-empty by anything in the file. Same shape as the 2026-07-20 BIN-513 "test name states a
  broader claim than the fixture actually samples" pattern, just at much lower stakes (static
  hardcoded strings, not derived logic). Fix is cheap: loop over all three ids and their
  returned entries, not just one.

Both are non-blocking here given the helper is pure curated display data with no runtime
derivation and trivial correctness risk — flagged for completeness, not filed as a defect.

a Cloud Function's business logic can be factored behind a narrow, 1-op-per-Firestore-call port
interface, that port can be satisfied by BOTH the Admin SDK (prod) and the modular client SDK
(test), unlocking real emulator coverage for code that would otherwise be stuck as
"review-gated, not test-gated" purely because `firebase-admin` isn't resolvable in the root/
rules vitest toolchain. This is a stronger technique than the existing `*.helpers.ts`/pure-logic
extraction pattern — it covers the LOOP (paging, error→audit→re-throw, cursor persistence),
not just the per-call predicates.

**Verified, not just read:** ran the real emulator (`npx firebase emulators:exec --only
firestore --project demo-binge-rules "vitest run --config vitest.rules.config.ts
src/test/rules/tmdb-sweep-orchestrator.test.ts"`) → 8/8 green. Hand-traced every assertion in
all 8 cases against `runSweep.ts` + `logic.ts` line-by-line (staleness-by-absence on

`watchlistDoc()` fixture, the scanned-but-neither-cleared-nor-skipped accounting for a
`groups/{id}/watchlist` doc via the bare `continue`, the dry-run-vs-mutate separate-cursor
bookkeeping across two sequential invocations) — all matched exactly. Also reran the untouched

functions` (clean) to confirm the extraction didn't regress anything neighboring. Attempted a

would catch it) but the harness's auto-mode classifier blocked the second emulator invocation
mid-session — noted as a limitation, not a finding against the diff, since the unmutated 8/8

### 2026-07-24 (later, same day) — SELF-CORRECTION: "faithful to the old call-site literals" is
NOT a proof of correctness. My earlier entry today approved the defect it was verifying against.

**What happened.** Earlier today I reviewed the `buildWatchlistAddPayload` extraction and logged
a PASS whose verification method was: "hand-traced each call site's pre-diff literal against its
post-diff call, field-by-field, to confirm the extracted `carry()` reproduces the exact same
`?? current?.x ?? fallback` chain the literal had." That trace was accurate — and worthless as a
correctness check, because the `?? null` / `?? []` chains in those literals WERE the bug. On a
`setDoc(..., { merge: true })` write, an explicit `null` DESTROYS the stored value while an
ABSENT key preserves it. So on a cold cache (`current` is null because the watchlist snapshot
hasn't settled) every carry fell through to its default and a plain status change wiped the
user's live rating and episode position. Today's later diff inverts the contract to "omit what
you don't know", and rewrites the test file I had approved.

**Rule (new, and the most important one in this log).** When reviewing an EXTRACTION or REFACTOR,
behavioural equivalence with the pre-diff code is the FLOOR, not the verdict. Ask the second
question every time: *is the behaviour being faithfully preserved actually correct?* Specifically,
for any helper whose output is fed to a Firestore `merge: true` write, adopt this checklist —
- a key present with `null` is a DELETE of stored data; a key ABSENT is a PRESERVE;
- therefore "fill every field with a default" is almost always wrong at a merge boundary;
- therefore any test asserting such a payload must use `toEqual` / `Object.keys`, never
  `toMatchObject` — a subset assertion is structurally blind to the only thing that matters.
The same trap recurred in the SAME session at the functions layer: `buildLastRunAudit` omitted
`error` on a clean run, and because `lastRun` is merge-written and Firestore DEEP-merges nested
maps, one failed run's `error: true` survived every later clean run. Two independent instances,
one root cause: **omission and null are not interchangeable at a merge boundary, and a test that
pins the wrong one of the two is a defect with a green checkmark.**

**Second correction, same file.** I also logged a PASS on `useOptimisticMirrorField.test.ts`
saying "all 10 assertions hand-traced ... discriminating". One of them was not: the test then
named "(account switch, 2026-07-20)" held `source` at the SAME object identity across the
rerender, so it exercised only the commit ref and never the mirror ref — the half that actually
leaked one user's subscription costs into the next user's profile (BIN-592). A test whose NAME
asserts more than its BODY does is a coverage lie that reads as coverage in exactly this log.
Rule: when a test name claims a scenario (account switch, sign-out, expiry), verify the fixture
actually VARIES the input that defines that scenario. Renaming such a test is a repair, not a
weakening — this round's rename plus a real replacement test is the correct pattern.

**Method note that caught all of it.** Mutation-testing, not reading, is what separated the three
honest changes from the one silent gap this round. Re-ran all three of the author's claims and
they were exact (3 / 2 / 1 failures), then ran two mutations the author had NOT claimed: the
per-chunk `onCommitted` accounting (emulator, 1 failure → discriminating) and — the one that
found something — reverting WatchlistContext's new conditional `addedAt` /
`tmdbFieldsRefreshedAt` stamping to unconditional, which left all 31 WatchlistContext tests
GREEN. That conditional stamping is the batch's only user-visible data-model change (the pure
helper cannot preserve anything by itself; `addItem` is what writes), and it drives the "Tillagd"
sort, backlogResurface, the GDPR export and the ToS sweep's freshness certification. **Standing
habit from here: when a batch's headline change is a pure helper, mutation-test the CALLER that
performs the side effect, not just the helper — the helper's tests can be immaculate while the
behaviour that reaches Firestore is entirely unpinned.**

**Third thing worth keeping: an honest "not testable" note beat a fake test.** The author
documented in-file that reverting the hook's `useIsomorphicLayoutEffect` to a plain `useEffect`
leaves the file green (RTL's `rerender` is act()-wrapped, so passive effects flush before any
assertion). I re-ran that mutation — true, 11/11 and 47/47 still green. Accept such notes, but
propose the repo's existing mechanism-guard escape hatch: `src/lib/design/consistency.test.ts`
reads source text with `readFileSync` + regex, and a 3-line guard pinning `useLayoutEffect` in
that file would fail on exactly the mutation that currently passes silently. A mechanism pin,
labelled as one, is legitimate where a behaviour pin is impossible.

**Contract (Malin, 2026-07-25, quoted in the diff's own code comment):** "har man manuellt
justerat 'sett' ska det bara andras om man sjalv manuellt andrar igen." Old code wrote
`watchedAt: serverTimestamp()` on every 'sedd' re-mark (stomping a backdated date on every
rewatch) and `watchedAt: null` on every non-'sedd' status (erasing history the moment a film
left 'sedd'). New code introduces a tri-state (`Date` = stored, don't touch; `null` = positively
known absent, safe to auto-stamp; `undefined` = unknown/cold-load, say nothing) via two new pure
exports: `resolveCurrentWatchedAt(current, snapshotSettled)` and `canAutoStampWatchedAt(v): v ===
null`. Both `buildStatusUpdate` (watchlistWrites.ts) and `WatchlistContext.addItem` call the SAME
`canAutoStampWatchedAt`, deliberately not reimplemented, so the two write paths can't drift.

edited to seed `currentWatchedAt: null` (previously absent/no such field). Verdict: LEGITIMATE.
Before BIN-593, `ctx.currentWatchedAt` didn't exist, so any call omitting it now resolves to
`undefined` under the new contract, meaning "unknown, don't stamp" — those tests would fail
against the new code unless the fixture explicitly signals known-absent (`null`) for the
"genuinely new / safe to stamp" scenarios they're asserting. The diff visibly implements the new
contract, no assertion was loosened (every changed assertion keeps `.toBe(TS)` / `.toBe(false)`
— same strictness, updated input), and net NEW tests are added for the harder tri-state cases.

## 2026-07-26 — BIN-595+BIN-596: required item discharged, `collectSettledFeed` extraction verified

Follow-up pass on the same batch (running alone). Diff since the 2026-07-26T00:16:23Z marker
touched only `src/app/feed/page.tsx` (blob f804ca2 → e506f6c) and `src/lib/feedTrending.ts` /
`.test.ts` (both new blobs, 9c211f5 / 192bb8f). Nothing else in the batch moved.

**What shipped:**
```ts
export function collectSettledFeed<T>(settled: PromiseSettledResult<T[]>[]): T[] {
  const fulfilled = settled.filter(
    (r): r is PromiseFulfilledResult<T[]> => r.status === 'fulfilled',
  );
  if (fulfilled.length === 0 && settled.length > 0) {
    throw (settled[0] as PromiseRejectedResult).reason;
  }
  return fulfilled.flatMap(r => r.value);
}
```
`feed/page.tsx` now calls `Promise.allSettled(...)` → `collectSettledFeed(settled).sort(...)`,
keeping only the sort inline. 5 tests appended to `feedTrending.test.ts` after the existing
`computeFollowTrending` describe (import line updated in place, nothing else in the file
touched): flatten-fulfilled-in-order, drop-only-failing-when-some-succeeded, throws-when-
all-failed, empty-input-is-empty, fulfilled-empty-is-not-a-failure. Total file: 12 `it(...)`.

**Mutations run (real file, restored from scratchpad backup each time, `git diff` empty +
suite green confirmed after each restore):**
1. Delete the whole `if (fulfilled.length === 0 && settled.length > 0) throw …` block →
   `1 failed | 11 passed` — fails exactly `THROWS when every entry failed`.
2. Narrow the guard to `if (fulfilled.length === 0)` (drop `&& settled.length > 0`) →
   `1 failed | 11 passed` — fails exactly `returns empty for an empty input`, via
   `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'reason')` on `settled[0]`
   (empty array has no index 0).
3. Extra mutation (not requested but needed to answer "are the two empty-case tests
   redundant"): check aggregate OUTPUT length instead of fulfilled COUNT —
   `const out = fulfilled.flatMap(...); if (out.length === 0 && settled.length > 0) throw …;
   return out;` → `1 failed | 11 passed` — fails ONLY `does not confuse a fulfilled EMPTY
   list with a failure` (throws `Unknown Error: undefined` because `settled[0]` there is a
   *fulfilled* result with no `.reason`). Confirms the two "empty" tests are NOT redundant:
   one pins "no input at all", the other pins "input resolved to nothing" — a plausible
   alternate implementation (check output length, not fulfilled count) flips only the
   second, so both earn their place.

**Style note surfaced, not blocked on:** `collectSettledFeed<T>` is a generic
`Promise.allSettled` collector with zero coupling to trending computation, dropped into a
file whose own header comment scopes it to "trendar bland personer du följer" aggregation.
The extraction satisfies the letter of the required finding (pure logic, no Firebase/RQ
coupling, sibling-directory precedent) but piggy-backs on the sibling's FILE, not just its
directory. Recommended (not demanded) it move to its own file next touch.

Other 6 batch files (WatchlistContext.tsx/.test.tsx, watchlistWrites.ts/.test.ts,
QuickAddButton.tsx, StatusButton.tsx) — sha-identical to the prior marker, not re-reviewed.

**Verdict:** PASS. Required item fully discharged, both named mutations reproduced exactly
as claimed, one voluntary extra mutation run to settle a scrutiny question the parent raised.
Marker re-stamped, all 9 reviewed files pinned to staged blob sha.

## 2026-07-29 — BIN-618: alias-collision fix in parseTmdbIdFromDocId (test-home split)

Reviewed (working tree, nothing staged): `src/lib/mediaTypeDocId.ts`, `src/lib/together/matching.ts`,
`src/lib/together/matching.test.ts`. Diff summary: `parseTmdbIdFromDocId` was tightened to (a) reject
leading-zero numeric suffixes (`CANONICAL_TMDB_ID = /^(?:0|[1-9][0-9]*)$/` replacing `/^[0-9]+$/`) and
(b) reject any underscore-containing doc id whose prefix isn't exactly `movie`/`tv` (old code sliced
after the FIRST underscore regardless of prefix, so `zmovie_42`/`season_5` silently aliased to the
genuine `movie_42`/`42` key). Documented and confirmed as a deliberate CLIENT-ONLY divergence from
`functions/src/shared/mediaTypeDocId.ts` (read that file — genuinely unchanged, old permissive regex
still there, matching the new client docstring's claim). `matching.ts` changed comment-only; no new
guard needed there because the alias now parses to NaN which never matches a real candidateKey.

Mutations traced by hand (pure regex/string-prefix change, no Firebase, desk-mutated against the
diff rather than live-run — same-file diff makes this reliable):
- `'movie_042'`/`'042'`/`'tv_0000042'`: old regex passes leading zeros -> 42; new one -> NaN. Flips.
- `'zmovie_42'`/`'season_5'`: old code ignores prefix entirely -> 42; new code short-circuits on the
  prefix guard -> NaN. Flips.
- matching.test.ts's 5 new BIN-618 cases (alias-after-genuine no-overwrite; unknown-prefix-vs-bare-id
  non-displacement; alias-alone forges nothing; alias doesn't get folded in as the BIN-608 legacy
  merge either — deliberately voting the alias-ONLY participant so BIN-608's merge can't mask the
  difference; alias doesn't count as swipe-progress) were each hand-run against the OLD parser and
  each flips to the wrong yes/no/vetoed/missing shape. Non-vacuous.
- The new `swipeFromDocId` test helper reproduces the REAL read path
  (`parseTmdbIdFromDocId`+`parseMediaTypeFromDocId`, matching `sessions.ts`'s `swipeDocToObject`
  exactly, confirmed by reading that function) rather than hand-rolling a parallel parse — the
  "mock/helper arity must track the real API" principle applied to a test fixture helper, not a mock.

Verdict: APPROVED, no assertion weakened/deleted/skipped. One non-blocking finding: the function's
OWN pre-existing paired unit-test file, `src/lib/mediaTypeDocId.test.ts` (with its own "Contract MUST
match..." header, i.e. exactly this codebase's canonical test-extraction home for this pure fn), was
NOT touched — none of the new leading-zero/unknown-prefix boundary cases were added there. Coverage
of the new invariant exists only inside `matching.test.ts`'s BIN-618 describe block (mixed
integration-via-`scoreCandidates`/`nextCandidate` style, plus one block of direct parser assertions).
The tests themselves are sound (see mutation trace above) so this isn't a coverage gap in the
blocking sense, but it IS a discoverability/maintenance gap: an editor who next changes
`mediaTypeDocId.ts` and reflexively runs its sibling `.test.ts` gets false-green on this exact
invariant. Folded into the active knowledge file's "Extract-then-test & layering" bullet (the "hook
file with no paired test" tell now has an explicit inverse: paired test file exists but wasn't
updated, with the slack picked up by a downstream consumer's file instead).

## 2026-07-29 — useStreamingOffers.test.ts (BIN-564): sound test, but staged as an EMPTY intent-to-add placeholder

**Scope:** review of `src/hooks/useStreamingOffers.test.ts` only (streaming area, BIN-564 —
legacy bare-id doc fallback for the movie/TV doc-id namespace split, BIN-523/560).

**Content review:** the file pins the exact bug the ticket describes — a pre-BIN-523
`streamingOffers/{tmdbId}` doc (bare id, shared by movie N and TV N) must resolve to "no
offers" when the caller's `mediaType` doesn't match the legacy doc's own `mediaType` field,
never to the other namespace's rows. Read `src/hooks/useStreamingOffers.ts` (the hook under
test) and `src/lib/streaming/offers.ts`/`src/lib/mediaTypeDocId.ts` (types + the pure doc-id
helper) for ground truth. Three cases: (1) legacy doc exists, wrong mediaType → `offers: []`,
`checkedAt: null`, both reads happen in order (namespaced-doc-id then bare-id) so the empty
result is the guard firing, not a read that never found the doc; (2) legacy doc exists,
matching mediaType (control) → serves it, proves the fallback path is reachable at all,
which makes case (1) non-vacuous; (3) namespaced doc exists → legacy is never read even
though a stale mismatched legacy doc also exists, proving the short-circuit.

**Mutation run:** edited the real `src/hooks/useStreamingOffers.ts` line
`return legacyDoc.mediaType === mediaType ? legacyDoc : null;` → `return legacyDoc;`
(dropping the mediaType guard entirely). Ran `npx vitest run
src/hooks/useStreamingOffers.test.ts --reporter=verbose`:

```
✗ returns no offers when the legacy bare-id doc belongs to the other media type
  expected [ { providerId: 8, … } ] to deeply equal []
✓ still serves the legacy doc when its own mediaType matches (control)
✓ never reads the legacy doc once a namespaced doc exists
```

Exactly the named test failed, and only it — the guard is genuinely load-bearing, the other
two are not incidentally coupled to it. Restored from a scratchpad backup
(`cp`'d before mutating), confirmed `git diff -- src/hooks/useStreamingOffers.ts` empty
afterward.

**Fixture/mock hygiene:** mocks only the documented choke point (`@/lib/firebase/db`'s
`fsdb`), leaves `mediaTypeDocId` real (pure, Firebase-free), asserts `readPaths` order —
matches the "mock the choke point, not the whole SDK" house rule and the
extract-then-test pattern (offer-shape logic lives in `src/lib/streaming/offers.ts`,
already covered elsewhere; this file is hook-wiring only, correctly not duplicating that
coverage).

**The actual defect found — a git-staging problem, not a test-content problem:**
`git status --porcelain` for this path prints `" A src/hooks/useStreamingOffers.test.ts"`
(space, then `A`). `git rev-parse :src/hooks/useStreamingOffers.test.ts` resolves to
`e69de29bb2d1d6434b8b29ae775ad8c2e48c5391` — git's canonical EMPTY-blob sha — while
`git hash-object src/hooks/useStreamingOffers.test.ts` (the real worktree content) is
`5f103447554260328bdbad1608d671c923d56e7d` (99 lines). `git cat-file -e
HEAD:src/hooks/useStreamingOffers.test.ts` fails ("exists on disk, but not in 'HEAD'"), and
`git diff --cached --raw -- <path>` returns **nothing at all** for this path (not even an
"A" line) — the fingerprint of an intent-to-add placeholder (`git add -N`, or an editor/IDE
integration doing the same), not a deliberately-staged empty file. Practical effect: as
currently staged, a `git commit` will NOT land the 99-line test authored in the working
tree — intent-to-add entries are excluded from a commit unless re-`git add`ed first.

**Verdict:** the authored test content is correct, discriminating, and well-scoped —
APPROVED on content. Filed as a Critical finding regardless, because the byte-for-byte
correctness of the working-tree file is irrelevant if the commit that ships won't contain
it. Fix stated to the requester: run `git add src/hooks/useStreamingOffers.test.ts` before
committing (not something this reviewer does on the coordinator's behalf, per house rule).
Marker pinned on the worktree `git hash-object` sha, with the staged/worktree delta named
explicitly, per the "nothing staged / mismatched staged blob" protocol.

**Lesson folded into the principles file (same edit):** extended the existing `MM`/
`M`+unstaged bullet in "Review protocol & scope discipline" to cover the `" A"` +
empty-blob-sha + empty `--cached --raw` diff signature of an intent-to-add placeholder,
since it's a variant of "staged blob ≠ working tree" the existing bullet didn't name.

## 2026-07-29 — BIN-609 watchlist read fail-closed against owner profile

**Diff reviewed:** `firestore.rules`, `src/test/rules/firestore-rules.test.ts`,
`docs/workflow-map.html` (unstaged working-tree changes, nothing staged for these three
paths — `git rev-parse :<path>` == HEAD blob for all three; worktree shas pinned instead).

BIN-609 (BIN-587 Option 2) adds two new rule functions, `profileAllowsPublic(uid)` /
`profileAllowsFriends(uid)`, and ANDs them onto all four `users/{uid}/watchlist/{itemId}`
non-owner read clauses (public / friends / legacy-isPublic-fallback / no-field-fallback).
Rationale in the rules comment: `effectiveVisibility` on the item is a denormalised copy
of the owner's profile `defaultVisibility`, stamped by `WatchlistContext` and cascaded by
`AuthContext.updateDefaultVisibility` (`cascadeVisibilityToItems`); if that cascade dies
partway (and BIN-587's own pending-flag repair can itself fail to persist), items keep
serving the OLD, more open value forever unless the read is also gated live against the
current profile — mirrors the existing `publicProfiles/{uid}` pattern (BIN-505).

**Test file:** a new `describe('BIN-609 watchlist read is fail-closed against the owner
profile')` block, 13 tests: the stale-public-goes-private leak (denied); public-while-
profile-public (still allowed); legacy isPublic-only profile (honoured); public item under
a friends-only profile (denied); owner always reads own item; friend denied once profile
goes private; friend allowed while profile still permits friends (+ non-friend still denied
— profile gate widens nothing); legacy isPublic-only item denied/allowed matching profile;
un-stamped item (neither field) follows profile both ways; profile doc gone entirely →
denied; and two BIN-595-interaction tests pinning that a per-item override can only NARROW
access, never widen past the profile (public override denied under private profile; private
override still hides under a public profile).

**Mutation run (house method, in-place on the real `firestore.rules` with a scratchpad
backup):**
1. `cp firestore.rules` → scratchpad backup, `diff -q` confirmed byte-identical.
2. Baseline: `firebase emulators:exec --only firestore --project demo-binge-rules "npx
   vitest run --config vitest.rules.config.ts --reporter=verbose -t BIN-609"` → 13/13 pass.
3. Edit tool reverted the four read clauses to their pre-BIN-609 text (dropped
   `profileAllowsPublic`/`profileAllowsFriends` entirely, restored the old direct
   `get(...).data.get('isPublic', false)` fallback clause) — a faithful revert-to-HEAD of
   just that block.
4. Re-ran the same filtered suite: **exactly 6 of 13 failed**, and only the 6 that name the
   new behavior: "DENIES a stale-public item once the profile has gone private (the leak)",
   "DENIES a public item when the profile is friends-only", "DENIES a friend a stale
   friends-item once the profile has gone private", "DENIES a legacy isPublic-only item once
   the profile is private", "DENIES everything when the owner profile doc is gone entirely",
   "a per-item public override does NOT out-rank a private profile (narrow-only)". The other
   7 (profile-still-permits cases, owner-always-reads, the private-override-still-hides
   case) passed under BOTH old and new rules, as expected — they were never claiming the new
   behavior.
5. Edit tool restored the original text verbatim; `diff -q` against the scratchpad backup
   confirmed byte-identical; `git diff -- firestore.rules | wc -l` == 70 both before and
   after (the real, intended diff, untouched).
6. Full `test:rules` suite (not filtered): 244/244 passed, 3 test files.
7. `node scripts/check-workflow-map.mjs` → "OK — 90 nodes, 28 flows, all referenced paths
   exist, coverage 61/61" — the workflow-map.html edit (new flow1 steps describing the
   visibility-cascade write path + BIN-587 repair leg, plus updated descriptions on the
   addItem/feed/Tillsammans-swipe flows for BIN-595/600/569/608) passes the linter and is
   consistent with the code it describes (spot-checked `visibilityRetriedFor` in
   AuthContext.tsx, `shouldStampVisibility`/`updateVisibility` split in watchlistWrites.ts).

**Verdict: APPROVED.** No weakened/skipped/deleted assertions found across the three
files. The new fail-closed gate is real (mutation-discriminating on exactly its own claims),
the BIN-595 override-interaction tests correctly pin narrow-only (never-widen) semantics
in both directions, and the workflow-map update is scoped to the touched flows and
passes CI's linter. Session note: mid-review, one `firebase emulators:exec` invocation was
denied by the auto-mode classifier while `firestore.rules` was mid-mutation (differed from
HEAD); an immediate retry of the identical command succeeded — treat this as a

`git show :path` against HEAD showed the STAGED version carries the full 7-line comment
verbatim but NOT the `visibilityRetriedFor.current = null;` line it explains — a partial

into the worktree (i.e. ran the suite against exactly what a bare `git commit` would ship),

```
× ... a fresh sign-in as the same uid gets a new auto-retry (the latch is cleared on sign-out)

Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  1 failed | 15 passed (16)
```

backup (`diff -q` byte-identical), re-ran: 16/16 green, `git status` back to the identical `MM`

before commit — no code change needed. Findings filed as Critical (process, not logic) per
the "MM" protocol. No new Critical/High logic issue in either file's content.

**Lesson folded into the principles file (same edit):** extended the existing "`MM` /
`M`+unstaged" bullet under "Review protocol & scope discipline" — added the specific
"comment lands, the line it explains doesn't" partial-hunk shape as a named instance, and
generalized the remedy to "swap `git show :path` into the worktree, run, note the flip,
restore" as the direct way to test whether the STAGED content (not just the worktree) would
pass CI. No new bullet was needed; this is a sharper instance of the same pattern the bullet
already named (distinct from the BIN-593/watchedAt precedent immediately above in this
archive, which was "index == HEAD, nothing staged at all" rather than a same-hunk split).

recurs PER VALIDATOR and the regression arrives when the READ side is added later; (2) a real
browser API written then read back with no production code between is as tautological as a mock
asserting itself, so check fixture ORDER; (3) mock arity means the real FIELD list, not just
params, and a mock missing a field makes the case named for it a subset of its sibling; (4) an
allowlist needs a fixture per MEMBER, not just per rejected value. Also recorded the two-step
stable-router diagnostic as the standing check for a "runs once" latch. Compressed the BIN-641
narrative bullets (intent-term, narrowing, UI-confirmation, extract-then-test), the sha/toolchain

## 2026-08-01 — BIN-657: global-error.tsx telemetry, sentry.ts's own contract left untested by a full-module mock

Scope: `src/app/global-error.tsx`, `src/lib/sentry.ts`, `src/app/global-error.test.tsx`
(infra-hygiene batch, reviewed alongside a concurrent watchlist/auth batch in the same
checkout — kept both named in the shared `test-done.marker` rather than overwriting).

Diff: `global-error.tsx` gained a `useEffect` that logs to console, awaits
`initSentry().then(() => captureError(...))`, and fires `trackEvent`. `sentry.ts`'s
`initSentry()` changed signature from `void` (fire-and-forget, `initStarted` boolean guard)
to `Promise<void>` (`initPromise` cache), so the caller can await the lazy `@sentry/react`
chunk before reporting — global-error.tsx replaces the root layout, so `Providers.tsx`
(which normally kicks off `initSentry()`) never mounts there.

`global-error.test.tsx` drives the transition properly (per the digest's "test the whole
transition, not just that a wait starts" lesson): renders, asserts `console.error` +
`trackEvent` fired synchronously and `captureError` did NOT fire yet, then resolves the
mocked `initSentry()` promise and asserts `captureError` fires with the exact payload.
Second test asserts the recovery UI (`reset` click). Both mutation-verified real:
- Reverting the await-then-report to a synchronous `captureError(...)` call before
  `initSentry()` settles reddened `expect(captureError).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` alone.
- `npx eslint` clean on all three files.

Gap found: the test mocks the WHOLE `@/lib/sentry` module
(`vi.mock('@/lib/sentry', () => ({ initSentry: ..., captureError: ... }))`), and it is the
ONLY test file in the repo that imports `@/lib/sentry` at all (grepped
`vi.mock\('@/lib/sentry'\)` across `src/`: 1 match). That means `sentry.ts`'s own
implementation — the DSN-empty/no-window early-`Promise.resolve()` branches, the real
`import('@sentry/react').then(...).catch(...)` chain, the `beforeSend` PII scrub
(strips `event.user.email/username/ip_address`, clears `event.request.url`'s query
string), and the catch-branch that resets `initPromise` to `null` for a retry — has ZERO
direct test coverage, before or after this diff.

Verified by mutation on the real file (backed up to scratchpad first, restored after,
confirmed via `git diff --stat` empty and `git rev-parse :<f>` matching the pinned staged
blob `1084dac0472b2125a3bf0e1856c3383cd21f48d8`):
```
if (!DSN) return Promise.resolve();   // no-op i dev/CI om DSN saknas
```
→
```
if (!DSN) { void 0; return undefined as unknown as Promise<void>; }
```
Ran `rm -rf node_modules/.vite/vitest && npx vitest run --reporter=verbose` (full suite,
2300 tests): 4 files / 8 tests failed, all in `StatusButton.test.tsx` /
`HomePageClient.test.tsx` etc. — files outside this review's scope. Confirmed these are
NOT caused by the sentry.ts mutation: restored `sentry.ts` (sha match re-verified) and ran
`StatusButton.test.tsx` alone → 9/9 green, consistent with cross-file test-order/shared-
mock pollution in the full run rather than a real defect touching the 3 reviewed files.
`global-error.test.tsx` alone, run against the mutated `sentry.ts`: still 2/2 GREEN —
because it mocks the module boundary, the mutation to the real file's branch never reaches
the test. In production this exact mutation would throw `undefined.then is not a function`
synchronously inside `global-error.tsx`'s own recovery `useEffect` — the LAST-RESORT crash
boundary throwing on its own reporting path — and nothing in the suite would catch it.

Verdict: **fail.** High-severity coverage gap (not a weakened/skipped assertion — a
same-commit contract change with no direct test of the file that owns it). Filed:
add `src/lib/sentry.test.ts` mocking only `@sentry/react`
(`vi.mock('@sentry/react', () => ({ init: vi.fn(), captureException: vi.fn() }))`, per the
existing "mock only the documented choke point" convention), driving: (1) DSN empty →
promise resolves, captureError no-ops after; (2) DSN set + import resolves → `S.init`
called with expected options, a post-resolution captureError forwards tags/extra; (3)
`beforeSend` strips the 3 PII fields and clears the URL query (GDPR-adjacent, currently
wholly unexercised); (4) import() rejecting → `console.warn` fires and a second
`initSentry()` call retries (`initPromise` reset to null). Folded into the knowledge file's
"mock only the documented choke point" bullet.

**Scope:** re-review of `src/hooks/useSubscriptionAdvisor.helpers.ts` +
`src/hooks/useSubscriptionAdvisor.test.ts` as staged in the working tree, after
automated fixes were applied earlier in the sprint.

**Diff reviewed:** adds `hasAiredNumberedSeason(show, airedFrontierDate)` (checks
`show.seasons` for any `season_number >= 1 && episode_count > 0 && air_date &&
air_date <= airedFrontierDate`) and one new branch in `isUserBehindOnAired`:
`if (userOnSpecials && hasAiredNumberedSeason(show, last.air_date)) return true;`,
placed after the existing "different tracks → true" guard so it only fires when
BOTH the user's marker and the aired frontier are on the specials track (S0) but a
numbered season has since aired — the BIN-589 hole BIN-615 was filed to close.
4 new test cases added, all additive (no assertion weakened, skipped, or deleted).

**Split-index check:** `git rev-parse :<f>` == `git hash-object <f>` for both
files both before and after mutation work — no split, no concurrent mover.

**Mutations run** (real prod file, `rm -rf node_modules/.vite/vitest` before each,
scratchpad backup restored + `diff -q` verified byte-identical + `git diff --stat`
empty after each):
1. `s.season_number >= 1` → `>= 0` (let S0 itself count as "a numbered season
   aired"): RED — caught by "keeps caught up… season has not aired yet" (S0 airs
   before the frontier, so >=0 wrongly flips it to behind).
2. Drop the `userOnSpecials &&` guard entirely (unconditional
   `hasAiredNumberedSeason` check): RED — caught by "leaves the numbered track
   untouched" regression guard.
3. `episode_count > 0` → `>= 0`: RED — caught by the "no air date or no episodes"
   case's `noEpisodes` half.
4. `s.air_date <= airedFrontierDate` → `s.air_date < airedFrontierDate`
   (same-day-exclusive instead of inclusive): **GREEN, 62/62 — gap.** No fixture
   sits ON the boundary; the "returns true" fixture's seasons air in 2021/2022
   against a 2024 frontier (well before), and the "keeps caught up" fixture's
   numbered season airs 2024-06-01 against a 2024-01-01 frontier (well after).
   Neither distinguishes `<=` from `<`.

**Also checked:** consumer wiring (`src/lib/watchStatus.ts` imports
`isUserBehindOnAired` from the same helpers file — single source of truth, no
duplicate copy to re-fix); the in-code comment's self-reference to
"useSubscriptionAdvisor.test.ts:336" resolves to the correct test; `tsc --noEmit`
and `npx eslint` on both files are clean; `accepted-deviations.md` has nothing
matching this surface.

**Verdict:** PASS. The boundary gap (mutation 4) is Medium, not blocking — a
same-day air-date collision between a numbered season's premiere and the last
aired specials episode is a narrow real-world edge case, and the code's own
comment states the inclusive intent ("samma dag eller tidigare"), so the
implementation is very likely correct even though untested at the exact boundary.
Filed as a fix suggestion, not a ship-blocker. Folded into the `>=`/`>` boundary
bullet in the principles file rather than added as a new one.

only fires once the section is expanded, filtering the live TMDB season-0 payload down to the

each mutation applied to the real file, run, restore via `cp` from a scratchpad backup, `git diff
--stat` empty confirmed after each restore.

   Result: `excludes the non-episode season-0 clutter it sits next to` failed ALONE (5/6 still

   unconditional render (drops the lazy-fetch gate). Result: both `does not fetch season 0 until
   the section is expanded` AND the collapsed-state assertion inside the first test failed (5/7
   still green) — the lazy-fetch contract is genuinely double-pinned.
4. `SeasonList.tsx`: the season-0-presence guard `seasons.some(s => s.season_number === 0) ?
   curated : null` → bare `curated` (drops the guard, always shows the section for a curated show
   even when TMDB lists no season 0 at all). Result: `skips the section when TMDB lists no season
   0 for a curated show` failed ALONE (6/7 still green).

All four mutations were caught by exactly the test their name promises, none of the four green-
alone shapes leaked into a sibling assertion. No weakened, deleted, or skipped assertions
anywhere in the diff — this is a wholly additive feature with all-new test files. Checked
`accepted-deviations.md`: nothing in this diff overlaps a listed deviation (not rules, not PII,
not money, not the tmdbTosSweep gate).

One Low, non-blocking finding: `isCanonicalSpecial` is exported and fully covered by its own test
file (6/6, including the negative "excludes clutter" and "false for uncurated show" cases) but is
never called from `SeasonList.tsx` — `CanonicalSpecialsPanel` re-derives the identical check
inline (`new Set(episodeNumbers); ep => allowed.has(ep.episode_number)`) instead of calling the

third inverse-extraction shape (tested-but-unconsumed export) rather than filed as its own ticket.

`useQuery` with React Query's default structural sharing, so `person`'s object reference only
changes when the fetched data is not deep-equal to the prior result. `svBio` reads only
`person.biography` and is recomputed fresh every render (not memoized independently) — it
cannot change value while `person`'s reference is unchanged, and cannot hold a stale value
against a changed `person` either. `[person]` alone subsumes it; the collapse is a redundancy
removal, not a dropped guard. No RTL harness demanded — this is a pure identity argument, not a
gate needing the transition-drive treatment (BIN-645's `profileLoading` lesson applies to a
mocked hook returning a FRESH object per call with independent state, not to a query-data field
with no independent source).

## 2026-08-02 — BIN-601/640 rebuild: dead-listener addedAt guard + read-side/repair fallback

**Diff reviewed** (staged): `src/lib/watchlist/addedAt.ts` (new, `hasStoredAddedAt` /
`resolveAddedAt` / `addedAtIsRepairable`) + `addedAt.test.ts` (new); `src/hooks/usePublicProfile.ts`
(exports `mapWatchlistDoc` for test, uses `resolveAddedAt`) + `usePublicProfile.test.ts` (new);
`src/contexts/WatchlistContext.tsx` (error callback on the watchlist `onSnapshot`, `listenerFailedRef`
gate on the `addedAt` stamp, a new own-effect repair pass keyed on `items` with its own
`repairedAddedAtRef` dedupe + `itemsUidRef` cross-account guard + chunked `writeBatch`) +
`WatchlistContext.test.tsx` (extended: `onSnapshot` mock grew a 3rd `onError` param, plus a new
`describe('WatchlistContext — dead listener: addedAt is neither destroyed nor faked (BIN-601/640)')`
block, 10 tests); `src/types/domain.ts` (`addedAtIsFallback?: boolean` on `WatchlistItem`). Plan +
Software Architect (#14) blind critique in `tasks/todo.md` lines 1026-1183 — the architect's ONE
blocking finding (mark-before-write via its own effect + in-progress ref + chunked batch, not a
write inside `onSnapshot`) was implemented; three of the architect's binding conditions (two-tab
test, exact-vs-drifts-on-second-touch honesty, batching) were each turned into a named test.

**Mutations run, cache cleared (`rm -rf node_modules/.vite/vitest`) before every run, every mutant
restored and `git hash-object` confirmed byte-identical after:**

1. Drop `|| listenerFailedRef.current` from the `addedAt` stamp gate → **1 failure** (`does NOT
   rewrite addedAt on a re-mark once the listener has failed`). Matches claim.
2. Error callback no longer sets `listenerFailedRef.current = true` → **1 failure**, same test.
   Matches claim.
3. Remove the repair effect's `itemsUidRef.current !== uid` cross-account guard → **1 failure**
   (`does not repair a previous account's rows on a same-session uid switch`), and the failure is
   the REAL leak — the write lands at `users/u2/watchlist/tv_7` carrying account A's date. Matches
   claim.
4. Remove `repairedAddedAtRef` marking entirely (never mark) → **1 failure** (`never repairs twice,
   even when the write failed and the field is still missing`). Matches claim. A SECOND variant —
   move the mark from before the async IIFE to inside the `try` block, after a successful
   `batch.commit()` — passed 65/65. Root cause: the test harness's `writeBatch().commit()` is
   hardcoded `async () => {}` (always resolves) regardless of what its own `set`/`update` calls
   return, so a real commit failure is unsimulable; only an unawaited/unobserved rejection from an
   individual `update()` call can be faked, and production code never awaits those individually.
   This is the exact retry-storm shape the architect's blocking finding was about, and it is
   currently unverifiable by any test in the suite — folded into the knowledge file's mock-arity
   bullet as a new clause. Low severity here only because the real mark sits synchronously before
   the whole async chain even starts (hardest possible placement to regress by accident).
5. Repair write also carries `updatedAt: it.addedAt` → **2 failures** (`repairs a doc that has no
   stored addedAt, writing ONLY addedAt` and `a second tab repairs independently`, both asserting a
   strict `toEqual({ addedAt: ... })`/`{ addedAt: updated }`). Matches claim.
6. `usePublicProfile`'s `mapWatchlistDoc` reverted to bare `toDate(data.addedAt)` → **2 failures**
   (`resolves a missing addedAt to the doc's own updatedAt`, `keeps an addedAt-less title OUT of the
   public 30-day counter`). Matches claim.
7. (Not separately claimed, checked anyway) Remove `listenerFailedRef.current = false;` from the
   successful-snapshot branch → **1 failure** (`resumes stamping once a snapshot proves the
   listener recovered`) — the recovery half of the guard is pinned too.
8. `addedAtIsRepairable`'s `&&` → `||` → **2 failures** in `addedAt.test.ts` itself (`is false when
   BOTH are missing` cases) — the pure helper's own boundary is pinned, not just its consumers.

**Attack-hardest targets, both cleared:**
- Same-session uid-switch test (`does not repair a previous account's rows...`): beyond mutation 3
  above, tried a DEAD-LOCK mutation (`if (itemsUidRef.current !== uid) return;` → `if (true) return;`,
  i.e. the guard never clears) — the test's own positive control (`snapshotCallback!(snap([...]))`
  for the new uid, then asserting the repair write for `u2` DOES land) failed with `expected [] to
  deeply equal ['users/u2/watchlist/tv_60']`. So the `view.rerender(...)` mechanism genuinely proves
  the guard DEFERS (fires once B's own snapshot lands) rather than merely happening to pass because
  the guard silently never re-enables.
- Two-tab test (`a second tab repairs independently — the bound is per session, not global`): the
  harness's `snapshotCallback` is a single module-scope `let`, overwritten by whichever
  `WatchlistProvider` instance mounted/subscribed most recently — so invoking it after tab B mounts
  drives ONLY tab B's `onSnapshot` handler, and each tab's `repairedAddedAtRef` is a `useRef` scoped
  to its own component instance (not module state), so the test's 2-calls assertion is real: a
  hypothetical module-level/shared dedupe Set would make tab B's repair see the doc as
  "already handled" (marked by tab A) and skip the write, dropping the call count to 1 and failing
  the test. Confirmed by reasoning through the mock's `let`-based routing (not separately mutated
  live, since there is no single-line mutation that converts a `useRef` to module scope without a
  larger refactor) — the test's own comment states the honest tradeoff ("same value, so harmless,
  but 'exactly one write ever' would be a false claim") rather than overclaiming exclusivity.

**Other items checked:**
- `mapWatchlistDoc` exported from `usePublicProfile.ts` "for test only", with a comment explaining
  the PUBLIC-read-path rationale — legitimate extract-then-test; BIN-640's whole point (a stranger's
  screen, not just the owner's) is only provable on this specific mapper.
- Multi-touch-during-outage test (`repairs a title touched TWICE during one outage to its LAST
  touch, not to now`) states the drift honestly (asserts the repaired `addedAt` equals the LAST
  touch's `updatedAt`, not the true original add time) — matches the architect's binding condition
  to "say this plainly rather than under-claiming" rather than papering over the cost.
- `git diff --cached --stat` and every reviewed file's `git rev-parse :<path>` re-checked
  immediately before writing this entry — unchanged from the start of the review. A CONCURRENT
  session was found live-editing `src/lib/watchlist/buildAddPayload.ts`/`.test.ts` (unstaged, a
  compile-time `ts-expect-error` pin keeping `addedAtIsFallback` off `WatchlistAddPayload`) during
  this review — out of scope (not staged, not part of this diff) and does not touch any of the
  reviewed files; noted for the parent agent, not filed as a finding.
- `.claude/rules/accepted-deviations.md` read in full; nothing in this diff matches an entry there.

**Verdict: pass (0 blocking).** One LOW finding (writeBatch().commit() mock cannot simulate a real
batch-commit failure, so the "mark before write, not after success" distinction is only proven
against outright-removal, not against the subtler post-commit-success placement) — folded into the
knowledge file's mock-arity bullet rather than blocking, since production code's actual placement
(synchronous, before the whole async chain) is the safest possible shape and not the shape that
regression would plausibly take.

`git hash-object` confirmed byte-identical to the index blob (`5a3be0fa...`). **Verified as
claimed — CLOSED**, folded into the knowledge file's mock-arity bullet (no longer a LOW finding).

**Claim 2 — `addedAtIsRepairable`'s `updatedAt != null` term / both-null echo case.** The
coordinator's comment says dropping the term fails 25 tests file-wide because unrelated seeded
docs without `updatedAt` become spuriously "repairable". Reproduced exactly: deleted the

ordinary add`, seeding `{addedAt: null, updatedAt: null}`) is redundant given that blast radius,
or earns its place. Ran a SECOND, narrower mutation to answer it: `!= null` → `!== undefined`
(treats an explicit `null` as "present", which only the Firestore latency-compensated
still-pending-`serverTimestamp()` echo produces — grepped the whole diff for `updatedAt: null`

dead-listener/repair cases stayed green. Restored, hash-verified. **Verdict: the dedicated test is
NOT redundant** — the 25-test number was collateral noise from the wholesale-deletion mutation,
not evidence about this test's own contribution; the narrow mutation is what isolates it, and only
the dedicated pair catches the realistic regression. Folded the general technique ("blast radius
from full-deletion mutation ≠ proof a new test is non-redundant; re-run with the term's own
boundary made precise") into the vacuous-oracle bullet.

honest, not decorative: nothing at runtime sets the field today (grepped — only the type system can
catch a future caller trying to carry it into the merge-write payload, which is exactly the
`notes`-shaped failure mode the file's own comment cites), and the directive is proven load-bearing

(would hand a private URL to the next account on a shared device, and BIN-669 lets a
remembered path survive onboarding). AuthContext adds isSigningOut() (a useRef-backed live
predicate, deliberately NOT consume-once per its own JSDoc) and wraps signOut in try/finally
to raise/lower a signingOutRef.

999 lines), OnboardingFlow.tsx/test.tsx, login/page.tsx/test.tsx, nextPath.ts.
.claude/rules/accepted-deviations.md read — nothing on this surface.

Q1 (mock fidelity, isSigningOut as live predicate not consume-once): verified faithful —
prod's own isSigningOut is the same shape. Mutation `if (!isSigningOut())` to `if (true)` in
AuthGuard.tsx, after `rm -rf node_modules/.vite/vitest`: 4/9 fail cleanly (exactly the 4
BIN-669 cases), restored from scratchpad backup, re-ran green 9/9. No test passes for the
wrong reason on this axis.

Q2 ("re-running the effect does not undo the skip" test): built a targeted mutant in
AuthGuard.tsx — `const consumedRef = useRef(false)` plus
`if (isSigningOut() && !consumedRef.current) { consumedRef.current = true } else { rememberNextPath(...) }`
(models a PER-INSTANCE consume-once bug, the exact shape the test's comment describes). Ran
the suite: 4/9 failed, including the FIRST BIN-669 test ("a deliberate sign-out leaves
NOTHING behind for the next account", a SINGLE render()/act() call, no rerender).
Investigated why a single mount already catches a per-instance latch bug: instrumented
AuthGuard.tsx with a module-level `export let __effectRunCount = 0` incremented at the top
of the guarded effect, wrote a throwaway src/components/__probe.test.tsx, rendered once —
__effectRunCount was 2 after ONE render()/act(). Mechanism: AuthGuard's own
`useEffect(() => setMounted(true), [])` forces a second render, and the file's
`useRouter: () => ({ push })` mock returns a fresh object every call, so the redirect
effect's router dep changes identity on that second render and re-fires. So every test in
the file, including plain single-mount ones, already exercises 2 runs of the guarded effect
for free. Consequence: the dedicated "re-running the effect" test (which calls
render(guard()) a SECOND time — a second INDEPENDENT mount, not rerender() of the first
instance) flips under the consume-once mutant, but never alone — it always co-fails with the
"a deliberate sign-out leaves NOTHING behind" sibling, which already double-fires
internally. Verdict: near-miss/subset (existing bullet 28 shape), not a coverage gap — the
behavior stays genuinely covered, just not by the mechanism the test's own comment claims
(framed as "React re-runs effects... Strict Mode... second pass", but what actually runs is
two separate first-mounts). LOW/non-blocking: rename-and-annotate candidate, not delete
(bullet 32 shape) — the fix is either naming the real mechanism or switching to an explicit
rerender() on one instance if within-instance re-execution is what's meant to be pinned.
__probe.test.tsx deleted, AuthGuard.tsx restored from scratchpad backup, diffed clean
against staged content (git diff --cached --stat matched original 26 ++/--).

  verified to not weaken any case, and it is what the plan doc's own BLOCKING acceptance

  this diff needed to be checked against or filed as a new deviation.

**Verdict: pass (0 blocking).** No weakened, deleted, or vacuous assertions found. The new
block's 9 denial cases are each individually load-bearing (verified as one atomic set, not
per-case, but the it.each structure means each fixture is its own oracle and the mutation

## 2026-08-05 — BIN-748 tab-handover marker + deleteAccount freshness gate + half-applied-plan retry

Reviewed staged diff (all index==worktree, confirmed clean before and after): `src/lib/tabSession.ts`
(new) + `.test.ts`, `src/components/AuthGuard.tsx` + `.test.tsx`, `src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx` +
`.test.tsx`, `src/components/settings/DeleteAccountSection.tsx`, `src/test/rules/account-deletion.test.ts`.

**tabSession.ts / tabSession.test.ts** — clean. `sessionStorage`-only marker (`binge:tabSession`),
read-only from the guard, written/retired by the provider. Tests pin: mark/retire round-trip,
sessionStorage-not-localStorage (load-bearing per the module's own doc-comment), a hand-planted
non-`'1'` value not counting, the private-mode throw→`true` asymmetry (with rationale matching the
source comment), writes never throwing, and a `vi.resetModules()` + re-import proving the answer
comes from storage and not a module-level var. No vacuity found.

**AuthGuard.tsx / AuthGuard.test.tsx** — the BIN-748 ref-latch `signedOutAtFirstVerdict.current =
!uid && !tabHasShownSession()` is exercised on BOTH terms: `bootSignedOut()` with `TAB_KEY` set vs
unset (each asserting the opposite `stored()` outcome), and the `!uid` term is covered indirectly by

the ref false regardless of the marker). The file's `useRouter: () => ({ push })` mock is a
fresh-object-per-call shape (the class the knowledge file flags as making dep-array terms inert) —
but the test file's own comment (lines 172-173) correctly identifies this and treats the resulting
extra effect-reruns as "belt", not the mechanism; the real driver is explicit `auth.loading`/`auth.uid`
mutation + `rerender()`, which the ref-latch reads regardless of `router` identity. Verified the
"waits for the auth verdict" test (starts-only) is paired with "arrives LATE" (drives the full
loading:true→false transition then asserts both push and stored()) — satisfies the BIN-645-class
"drive the whole transition" bar. No mutation run against this file this round (reasoned from
structure + the adjacent AuthContext+AuthGuard integration describe block, which does exercise the
same ref-latch end-to-end); flag for a follow-up round if this file is touched again.

**AuthContext.tsx `deleteAccount` freshness gate — REAL GAP, verified live.** Code:
`sessionAgeMs = Date.now() - new Date(authTime).getTime(); if (!(sessionAgeMs < RECENT_LOGIN_MAX_AGE_MS)) throw`.
Deliberately negated (not `>=`) so an unparsable `authTime` → `NaN` → `NaN < MAX` is `false` →
negated `true` → refuses, per the source comment. `AuthContext.test.tsx`'s new describe block
(`deleteAccount checks session freshness before erasing`) has fixtures at `minutesAgo(30)`,
`minutesAgo(10)`, `minutesAgo(1)`, and the unparsable-string case — none AT the exact
`RECENT_LOGIN_MAX_AGE_MS` (2:00) boundary. Mutation run: backed up `AuthContext.tsx`
(`git hash-object` f152d6e0…), changed line 988 `sessionAgeMs < RECENT_LOGIN_MAX_AGE_MS` →
`sessionAgeMs <= RECENT_LOGIN_MAX_AGE_MS` (mutant test on the mutant present before AND after the run,
same command), `rm -rf node_modules/.vite/vitest`, `npx vitest run src/contexts/AuthContext.test.tsx`
→ **32/32 GREEN, mutant survived**. Restored from the scratchpad backup, `git hash-object` matched
f152d6e0… again, `git status --porcelain` clean. This is the boundary-completeness bullet's pattern
exactly (`>=` vs `>`, staleness predicate) wearing a "we already handle NaN correctly" disguise — the
NaN-safety property and the boundary-DIRECTION property are two separate claims about the same `<`,
and only the first has a fixture. Folded into the active knowledge file's boundary bullet in place
(same edit) rather than appended, since it's the same bullet's pattern with a new disguise. Filed as
a blocking finding in the review (session-freshness gate on an irreversible-deletion pre-flight check
is a correctness-critical surface, and the exact-boundary case is exactly the ambiguous "was this
really under or over 2 minutes" click a real user could produce).

**account-deletion.test.ts, "a retry after a HALF-applied plan converges" — genuine, not vacuous.**
Read start to finish. The test builds the real plan via `collectDeletionRefs`, commits only

leaves a half-applied state and proves the retry converges" — not read as satisfied on the docstring's

**Verdict: fail (1 blocking)** — the `deleteAccount` freshness-gate exact-2-minute boundary. All

## 2026-08-05 — BIN-748 round 2: boundary fix verified, marker-scope tests verified, one duplicate test found

Round-2 re-review of the same BIN-748 diff after the round-1 blocking finding (missing exact-boundary
fixture at `RECENT_LOGIN_MAX_AGE_MS`) was fixed, plus a production redesign the integration reviewer
flagged in the same window: the tab-session marker changed from a boolean the provider retired to a
PATHNAME it never retires (`src/lib/tabSession.ts`), because a boolean flag could be gone by the time
a catch-all-router page's `AuthGuard` mounts (a commit or two after `loading` settles, via
`next/dynamic`). Reviewed files, all opened with Read: `src/lib/tabSession.ts`,
`src/lib/tabSession.test.ts`, `src/components/AuthGuard.tsx`, `src/components/AuthGuard.test.tsx`,
`src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx`, `src/contexts/AuthContext.test.tsx`, `src/lib/authErrors.ts`,
`src/components/settings/DeleteAccountSection.tsx`, `src/test/rules/account-deletion.test.ts`. Also
read `src/lib/firebase/accountDeletion.ts` (unstaged, verification target only).

**Mutation 1 — the round-1 fix, re-verified.** `AuthContext.tsx` line 987: `sessionAgeMs < MAX` →
`sessionAgeMs <= MAX`. `rm -rf node_modules/.vite/vitest` first. Ran
`npx vitest run src/contexts/AuthContext.test.tsx --reporter=verbose`: exactly 1 failure, "the cutoff
itself is refused, one millisecond younger is not" (33 passed). Restored from scratchpad snapshot,
`diff -q` byte-identical, `git diff` against the staged index empty. Confirms the fix and the new
frozen-clock (`vi.spyOn(Date, 'now')`, `Date.UTC` anchor) boundary fixture are real.

**Mutation 2 — `AuthGuard.tsx` line 48, the marker-check term.**
`signedOutAtFirstVerdict.current = !uid && !tabShowedSessionOn(...)` → `= !uid` (the pre-BIN-748
behavior). Ran `AuthGuard.test.tsx`: 4 failures — "remembers NOTHING when this tab had already shown
a session on this page", "also drops a path an earlier tap left in this tab", "holds even when the
guard mounts LONG after the verdict landed", "the very next guarded page is a bounce again, with the
marker untouched" (13 passed). The three sibling cases and the "late mount" case fail IN LOCKSTEP —
see the informational finding below. Restored, verified byte-identical, verified empty diff vs index.

**Mutation 3 — `tabSession.ts` line 66, the per-page scoping.** `return stored !== null && stored ===
normalize(pathname)` → `return stored !== null` (marker silences every page, not just the one it was
set on). Ran all three test files together: 6 failures across `tabSession.test.ts` (4: the per-page
unit tests, the empty-value test, the reload-reads-storage test), `AuthGuard.test.tsx` (1: "the very
next guarded page is a bounce again, with the marker untouched"), `AuthContext.test.tsx` (1: "the
marker silences ONE page, not the rest of the tab"). Both cross-file "silences ONE page" tests
(AuthGuard.test.tsx and AuthContext.test.tsx) are real, independent proofs of the BIN-645-funnel-
survival claim — confirmed by mutation, not inherited from the docstring. Restored + verified.

**Mutation 4 — `AuthContext.tsx` line 552, the write-effect dep array.** `}, [uid, pathname]);` →
`}, [uid]);` — dropping `pathname` so a same-uid navigation doesn't re-run `markTabSession`. Ran
`AuthContext.test.tsx`: exactly 1 failure, "the marker follows the session as the user navigates" (33
passed). Restored + verified.

**Mutation 5 — `src/lib/firebase/accountDeletion.ts` line 197, `fallbackUsername`.**
`?? fallbackUsername ?? null` → `?? null`. Full emulator control run first (`npm run test:rules`,
Java/JBR on PATH): 245/245 green. Mutated, reran: exactly 1 failure, "a retry after an INTERRUPTED
plan converges to the same end state", at the specific assertion `expect(await exists(['usernames',
MY_NAME]), 'username reservation released').toBe(false)` — 244/245 otherwise green. Confirms the
task's specific question: the interim `await runDeletion()` (no fallback, asserting the reservation
stays ORPHANED) is exactly what makes the fourth argument load-bearing, not decoration — without that
step the test would pass with the argument deleted (the second `runDeletion(MY_NAME)` call alone
would still converge if `collectDeletionRefs` had a fallback stored elsewhere, but here it does not,
so the mutation is the direct proof). Restored + verified byte-identical + `git diff` empty.

**Finding (informational, not blocking): AuthGuard.test.tsx's "holds even when the guard mounts LONG
after the verdict landed" does not discriminate from its sibling "remembers NOTHING when this tab had
already shown a session on this page".** Both fail together under mutation 2 above, never one without
the other, because `AuthGuard`'s ref-latch (`signedOutAtFirstVerdict.current === null`) has no memory
of how many renders preceded the first one where `loading` is false — mounting straight into
`loading:false` (this test) and transitioning from `loading:true` to `loading:false` via `bootSignedOut()`
(the sibling) hit the identical code on the qualifying effect run. The test's narrative — reproducing
DynamicRouter's late `next/dynamic` chunk-load mount — describes something real about the PRODUCTION
ordering (the marker's whole raison d'être, per `tabSession.ts`'s own doc comment) but the test itself
adds no incremental coverage over the sibling in THIS component, because there is no retirement/timing
state left in the code for a late mount to matter to. Folded into the existing knowledge-file bullet
on the BIN-645 `redirectedRef` "second render proves nothing new" pattern rather than filed as a new
bullet — same shape, different trigger (no rerender needed here, just a render that starts already
past the state a rerender would have reached).

**Verdict: pass (0 blocking).** The round-1 finding is genuinely fixed and independently reproduced.
The production redesign (pathname marker, never retired) is real, well-motivated by the DynamicRouter
mount-order defect, and its two load-bearing claims (per-page scoping; write-side dep-array
completeness) are both mutation-verified, not merely narrated. The one new observation is
documentation-quality, not a coverage gap — the underlying invariant remains covered by the sibling
test, so no follow-up ticket is warranted.

### The fake-timer hang test's cascading-failure signature — judged ACCEPTABLE, not a defect
Did not re-run this mutation (2026-08-10b already did, live: bare-`await` reversion times out at
5010ms as the FIRST failure, red-alone and unambiguous, then cascades ~20 more from the abandoned
`vi.useFakeTimers()` state). Judgment on the open question ("should it fail more precisely?"): the
cascade is a structural property of testing an unbounded hang with fake timers, not a test-quality
defect to fix — a suspended async function's `finally` cannot run before its awaited promise
settles, so nothing short of a REAL (unfaked) escape-hatch timer captured before `vi.useFakeTimers()`
could bound it, and even that would only localize the FAILURE, not prevent the fake-timer leak to
siblings (the leak is what the `finally` was for, and the finally never gets to run in the mutant
world by construction). The signature is diagnosable as-is: the timeout fires on the mutated test
by name, first in the list, at a suspicious round number (5010ms ≈ vitest's default 5s timeout) —
an engineer reading the CI output sees THIS test's name before the 20 that follow. Not filing a
change; noting the reasoning here so a future reviewer doesn't re-litigate it from scratch.

Restored from the (this time genuinely clean) backup, re-confirmed sha match, clean control: 37/37.

**Is "a throwing reporting callback" a real failure mode or coverage theater on a `logger.error` that will never throw?** Judged real, non-blocking either way: (a) `revokedUidsInBatches` is a general-purpose pure function taking an INJECTED `onBatchError` port — nothing in its own contract assumes the caller always passes `firebase-functions/v2`'s `logger.error`, so defending the function's own invariant ("a batch that throws contributes NO uid, no matter how the failure is reported") against an arbitrary injected callback is honest coverage of the function's actual signature, not a contrived scenario bolted onto today's one caller. (b) This is not a novel defensive shape for this codebase — the security reviewer's own knowledge file already generalizes the identical pattern ("the unit's own error-REPORTING callback needs its own nested try/catch too … an unguarded `onError?.(err)` inside the per-unit catch defeats the very isolation the outer try/catch exists for") citing this same fix, so it is recognized house discipline, not one-off padding. (c) `logger.error` itself is unlikely but not provably incapable of throwing (oversized structured-log payloads, a malformed metadata shape, a closed/errored stream during instance shutdown) — low-probability, not zero, and the blast radius if it did throw pre-fix (discarding already-revoked uids from earlier successful batches, on the ONE sweep in this file whose false positive/negative touches a LIVE account) justifies a one-test, ~15-line guard. Not blocking to have shipped it, and not something Malin should feel obligated to strip for leanness.

**`skippedAuthBatches: -1` sentinel**: judged against the round-2 precedent (a pass-through field into an untestable `index.ts` `logger.info` call needs no dedicated pin when every sibling count field in the same log call is equally unpinned under the file's accepted admin-import-blocks-root-vitest gap-class). The `0`→`-1` change does not alter that judgment — it is still pure plumbing with no branch or transform reachable from root vitest, just a clearer three-state sentinel (`-1` scan-died, `0` clean run, `>0` some batches skipped) replacing an ambiguous two-state one. No test owed, same reasoning as round 2, re-stated rather than re-litigated.

**Mid-review mover, informational, out of scope**: `.claude/agents/binge-security-reviewer.knowledge.archive.md`'s worktree diverged from its staged index sha (ee8acc9… vs 72b85f6…, the sha I read and confirmed matched at the start) partway through this review — a sibling security-reviewer session appending its own round-3 entry live. The staged INDEX content (already read in full, unchanged) is what this verdict is pinned to; the sibling's in-progress addition is not part of this diff's reviewed bytes and is not this review's concern.

Full suite: `npm test` → 2916 passed / 235 files / 4 skipped, matches the handed-down number exactly (ran myself). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean at root and `functions/` (zero output, both). `accepted-deviations.md` re-read in full: no entry applies.

**Verdict: pass (0 blocking)**. ## 2026-08-10 — BIN-848 round 3: `checkedUids`, a second passthrough field into the same untestable log line

**Diff reviewed** (`git diff --cached`, two files): `functions/src/retentionCleanup/index.ts` adds a
`checkedUids` field to `collectRevokedPushTokens`'s return type (JSDoc explains why: without it, a
run that checked nothing — no `fcmTokens` docs at all, or the scan died — is indistinguishable from
a healthy run that checked everyone and found them all live, which is exactly the reading the
post-deploy permission check depends on). Three write sites, mirroring `skippedAuthBatches`'s
existing three: `byOwner.size === 0` early return → `checkedUids: 0`; the end-of-function success
return → `checkedUids: byOwner.size`; the outer `Promise.all(...).catch()` handler in the exported
`onSchedule` body (scan died entirely) → `checkedUids: 0`. `tasks/todo.md` is rewritten to require
**both** `skippedAuthBatches: 0` AND `checkedUids > 0` before treating the sweep as live, with the
vacuous-early-return failure mode spelled out (the reason `skippedAuthBatches: 0` alone can lie).

**No test file changed.** `functions/src/retentionCleanup/logic.test.ts` is untouched (still 37/37,
confirmed by running it) and no new test file was added anywhere.

**Question asked**: is that omission honest, or does `checkedUids` deserve different treatment from
its sibling `skippedAuthBatches` — round 2's identical shape, archived above and folded into the
active knowledge file's retentionCleanup bullet — because THIS field is now load-bearing for a
written human verification step (the `tasks/todo.md` gate), where the sibling counts in the same
`logger.info` call (`expiredSessions`, `deletedSessions`, etc.) are pure telemetry nobody reads a
decision off of?

**Verdict reached: no escalation, same reasoning as round 2, non-blocking.** The applicable
discriminator (already stated in the active knowledge file for `skippedAuthBatches`) is not "does a
human decision depend on this field" — `skippedAuthBatches` already gated that exact same
`tasks/todo.md` verification step, alone, before `checkedUids` existed, and was accepted anyway. The
real discriminator is whether the field BRANCHES or re-derives new logic versus trivially forwarding
a value that already lives inside the file's accepted-gap pagination boundary. `checkedUids` is
`byOwner.size` — the size of the exact Map whose CONSTRUCTION (the `collectionGroup('fcmTokens')`
pagination loop + `d.ref.parent.parent?.id` owner-uid derivation) is the specific piece already
graded non-blocking in round 2's archive entry, for the specific reason that a pagination bug there
is uid-VALUE-keyed and cannot misattribute a revocation to a live account. Reading `.size` off that
same Map introduces no new branch and no new derivation; it is pure plumbing of a value that was
already in scope, exactly like `skippedAuthBatches` forwarding `skippedBatches` from the
mutation-tested `revokedUidsInBatches`. The three write sites were traced by hand (index.ts:214,
228, 299) and each assigns the value the docstring claims — no site swaps in a wrong variable
(e.g. `revoked.length`, which would silently degrade the new field to "some accounts were revoked"
instead of "some accounts were asked about," inverting its whole purpose) — verified by reading, not
by test, since none exists to run.

branch into that same pure layer would make it directly testable at near-zero marginal cost — but
that is riding along with a hypothetical future refactor of the untested pagination half, not
something owed by this diff alone.

  per-line-split string (no embedded `\n`) the two forms produce IDENTICAL results for every

   verified round 2). Traced the mechanism by hand: a watchlist doc with a non-numeric `tmdbId`
   (rules whitelist the key, never bind its type) makes `resolveTmdbId` fall back to the doc id,
   which is `NaN` for anything without a digits-only suffix; such an item is pushed into the work
   set every run, can never be fetched successfully, never gains `checkedAt`, and therefore never
   leaves tier-0 ("never checked", sorted first) — a permanent one-slot-per-run quota drain, the same
   failure shape BIN-856's headline bug had (though smaller — one item, not nine).
   **Recommendation: fold `Number.isFinite(item.tmdbId)` into `isIntentTitle` in `logic.ts` rather
   than leaving it at the call site.** Grounds: (a) `isIntentTitle` has exactly ONE caller (grepped
   `isIntentTitle` across `functions/src` — the import in `index.ts` and the test file are the only
   other hits), so folding the AND-term in is behaviour-preserving with zero divergence risk; (b)
   `isIntentTitle` already receives the full `IntentItem`, which carries `tmdbId` — no signature
   change; (c) `logic.test.ts` already has a five-case `describe('isIntentTitle', ...)` block, so the
   new case (`item({tmdbId: NaN})` -> `false`) costs one `it`, not a new test file or harness; (d)
   this is a direct instance of the "separate the stuck I/O from the extractable decision" principle
   (BIN-463/464) and `code-style.md`'s test-extraction convention — the guard IS a decision ("is this
   item eligible for the work set"), not I/O. Did not implement the move myself (review scope, not
   build scope) — flagged as a MED, non-blocking, cheap-to-close recommendation, named explicitly per
   the task's instruction to say so plainly rather than merely noting the gap. Folded into the
   principles file (bullet 64) as a concrete worked instance.

   !== 429) logger.error(...); else logger.warn(...)`. Traced control flow: the function's own
   preceding `if (res.status === 429) { rateLimited = true; break; }` already exits the loop (not a
   `continue`) before this block runs, so `res.status !== 429` in the new condition is provably

test `'names every one of those scripts in the BLOCKING list too (BIN-864/873)'` added).
This pass's own diff (verified via the isolated hunk in `git diff --cached`) is a pure
`//`-comment block inserted directly above the `GATE_SCRIPTS` declaration:

```

// is checked — measured: dropping an entry leaves the suite green, because no sibling
// test names any of these files against the commit gate. Removing a path here silently
// removes its blocking-side coverage, which is the same self-clearing move the array was
// hoisted to prevent. A file leaves this list only when it also leaves BOTH real lists.
```

No assertion line, no test body, no fixture changed in this hunk.

`771a5c9754cc0ee2706a482943dcce0938dbffe3` (index == worktree, no drift) before starting.

node_modules/.vite/vitest` then `npx vitest run docs/org --no-cache`:

```
Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  37 passed (37)
```

(clean control, same command pre- and post-mutation, was 38/38.) Confirms the comment's
own "measured: dropping an entry leaves the suite green" claim is accurate — verified
live, not inherited. `grep` across the file for the eight filenames confirmed none is
named by any test other than via `GATE_SCRIPTS` itself, supporting "no sibling test names
